summary: Tooltip is a toolbar of icon buttons whose labels appear after a short pause and then follow the pointer from button to button without waiting again. Avatars at the end open a larger card about each person, including the agent, with what they are doing right now. It shows a team and its agent working side by side in the same file.
use: When a toolbar is all icons and each one needs a name and a keyboard shortcut
When people and agents share a workspace and you want to show who is doing what
When an agent's presence should read as a teammate, with its own status line
When onboarding should point at a specific control by showing its tip on cue
features: Tools come in `groups`, with a thin divider between each group.
Each tip shows the tool's `tip` text, or its `label`, plus an optional `kbd` shortcut.
The first tip waits a moment, and moving straight to the next button shows its tip at once.
Hovering an avatar opens a person card after `cardDelay` ms, 300 by default, with name, role and status.
A person marked `working` shows the agent's thinking dots instead of a green dot.
`openTip` and `openCard` show a tip or card by key from your own code, for a guided tour.
a11y: Each icon button gets its `label` as an `aria-label`, and avatar buttons are named with the person's name.
Tips render with `role="tooltip"` and also open on keyboard focus, not only on hover.
Person cards open when an avatar receives keyboard focus and close on blur.
The card is marked `aria-hidden` while it is not showing.

faq.q: Can the label read differently from the button's accessible name?
faq.a: Yes. `label` is the name screen readers hear, and `tip` is the visible tooltip text when you want it to say more, like "Ask the agent" for a button named "Ask agent".

faq.q: How do I show what the agent is doing in the person card?
faq.a: Add the agent to `people` with a `status` like "Auditing contrast, 2 of 6 checks" and set `working: true`. The card then shows the thinking dots next to the status.

faq.q: How do I open a tip from code, for a walkthrough?
faq.a: Set `openTip` to the tool's key, or `openCard` to a person's key. Clear it to close, and leave it undefined to let the pointer decide again.
